lines.text: impart to him his true life, and then only as a gift if he
stands ready and available for the future, for what God
designs with him.
But who is there who can be thus ready for the future
which God gives? Who is so free from anxiety that he ceases
to cling to the transitory and perishable? Who is free from
his own past, from himself?
There is only one power which can free us from the bond-
age of self, and take away from us both our fear and our
self-despair. It is the power of love.
Through our human intercourse and dealings with each
other, whenever our common life is struck by the beams of
divine love, we know what the spirit and sway of love can
mean. And some of us are aware with shame and gratitude
that we are not what we have made of ourselves but what the
love that we have encountered, and that has been bestowed
on us, has enabled us to become. This mysterious power and
grace of genuine love rests upon this fact, namely that it sees
and understands and deals with a human being whom it
encounters, not as what he in effect at present is, but as
what he can and should and would like to be, as the being
whom he will be. It cheers and enheartens us when we
perceive that others are treating us as those whom we shall
be; it is an inspiration to us to see that the other can pene-
trate beyond all that is outward, beyond the grime of daily
life, the petty and trivial, the imperfect, the half-hearted
that adheres to each one of us; that the person with whom we
are dealing trusts us. And to trust a man means of course to
believe in his future. Such trust inspires the one who experi-
ences it with new happiness and sense of freedom.
Thus love bestows a real creative future and at the same
time belief in its unbounded horizons. But all our love is
only a faint reflection of the love of God, which "moves sun
and stars". How feeble and wavering is our power to give
and awaken love! Yet the essential message of Christianity
is that the love of God has been manifested in Jesus Christ.
